2. The petitioners filed an application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Keshabpur, (Jessore), being Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1987, stating, inter alia, that the petitioners are co-sharers to the case jote by inheritance while the pre-emptees are strangers, who purchased the case land from opposite party Nos.6-8 by a registered kabala dated 7-10-1984. It has been asserted that no notice of the impugned sale was served upon the petitioners and they came to learn about it for the first time on 2-1-1987 and hence the case on making the statutory deposit. 

 11. Mr. Nondy in support of his contentions has referred to the case of Abdus Sanuul and others vs. Md. Sohrab Ali and others reported in 33 DLR (AD), 113 wherein their Lordships have held that the object of sub-section (2) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is to have all the co-sharer tenants and all the tenants holding lands contiguous to the land transferred, before the court for proper and complete adjudication of the case. In the facts and circumstances of the case, I am in respectful agreement with the proposition of law laid down by their Lordships. 

 12. For the reasons stated above, I hold that the learned Assistant Judge erred in law in rejecting the petitioners' application for amendment of the pleadings by way of addition of a party without properly considering the scope of Order 6 rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and section 96(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the same has resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The impugned order is, therefore, liable to be setaside in the interest of justice.
